content.text: {"headline":"No action needed: service level is predicted at 91.5% for 15:15-19:45, above the 80% target, at no extra cost.","why":"Payments demand is running 27.5% above forecast all day (2,461 calls vs 1,930 expected) with no clear cause, and phone staffing dipped to 18 and 22 against 27 planned. Even so, the forecast for the disruption window is 91.5% overall (payments 87.7%, general 98.8%) with 1.5% abandons, and 91.8% for the rest of the day. Because the target is already met, the cheapest compliant plan is to leave staffing as it is.","trade_offs":["P1 (lend 2 general agents plus evening callbacks, no cost) gives the same 91.5% overall and lifts payments only slightly to 88.1%, while general drops to 98.0%.","P2 (₹360) reaches 92.4% overall and 89.4% on payments, a small gain for some disruption to general (98.2%).","P3 (₹3,600 overtime) gives the biggest improvement: 96.5% overall, 95.0% on payments, abandons down to 0.7%, and general is left untouched (99.2%). It costs ten times as much as P2.","P4 (₹1,440) gives 94.3% overall and 92.2% on payments, but takes 2 agents from general."],"watch":"The cause of the surge is unknown, and +53% in the 15:00 interval is above the all-day +27.5%. If volumes keep climbing or payments drops toward 80%, revisit P2 or P3. Also check adherence and breaks: agents on the phones were 18 and 22 against 27 planned, but only 1 absence is logged."}
